title: Imitation crab pasta

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
8 oz imitation crab, pulled into bite-size strips
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt. Cook the pasta until al dente. Save 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook 1 min, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the crab and cook 2 min, stirring gently, just until warm. It's already cooked, so it only needs heating.

For the pesto version, take the pan off the heat and stir in the pesto; cooking pesto turns it dull and oily. For the cream version, pour in the cream, simmer 2 min, then take it off the heat and stir in the parmesan until smooth.
Add the pasta and ¼ cup pasta water and toss until coated. Add more water if it looks dry.
Squeeze in the juice of half the lemon, season with salt and pepper and toss. Cut the other half into wedges to serve.
tips: Imitation crab is made from cooked fish, so long cooking makes it rubbery. Add it near the end.
Add 1 cup frozen peas to the pasta pot for the last 2 min for color.
storage: Fridge up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a skillet over low heat with a splash of water or milk. Don't freeze.
